groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Thanks for inviting me out tonight. I've been wanting to try this place for weeks. I usually pass it on my way home from work but never seem to have time to stop.
W: I've been dying to come here as well. I was worried that the menu might not be accommodating. But one of my close friends ate here last week. She's a vegetarian. She told me that there were a lot of options for her, and they offered alternative dishes.
M: But you're not vegetarian, are you?
W: Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs.
M: Isn't that very difficult? I can't imagine giving up a premium juicy steak or bacon cheeseburgers.
W: I wouldn't know. My parents followed the same diet. Even when I was younger, we never had meat during meals, and I never really had a craving to try it. I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating. I tried cutting back on coffee in the morning, and it was awful. Come to think of it, it was probably even worse for my colleagues that had to deal with me at morning meetings.
M: That's even harder to imagine you, without coffee. So you say your parents also followed a partially vegetarian diet? Why did they decide to do that?
W: That's an interesting question. I never thought to ask them though. My best guess is for health reasons. They're not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts, but they're serious about their health. Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick.
M: In that case, I might give it a try someday.
W: Now back to the menu. What are you going to have?

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: How did your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager go? Did you get much in the way of praise?
M: Next to zero. When we came to the part about discussing my areas for growth, he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. But he wouldn't really expand on that description. He said it's the little things I do and say.
W: Did you ask him for a specific example?
M: I did ask him a few more questions to try and narrow it down. He said my constant questioning of him and his decisions was the most obvious example he could give. Then our conversation was swiftly brought to a close.
W: I had a similar experience once. My manager told me I was too honest. In most cases, I thought my honesty was helpful, as did my colleagues, but my manager thought otherwise. Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict or complaints about unfairness.
M: Right. Some employ their persuasive vocabulary and influential communication style to win workplace arguments by compelling people to perform the intended action.
W: Exactly. Too honest? Isn't that a good thing? I thought that's surely something we should have covered earlier in the section discussing strengths and talents, but no. Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable, or at least it made the most powerful folks feel uncomfortable.
M: Indeed. Rhetoric is viewed by many philosophers as the method through which the powerful accumulate more power. By virtue of having the loudest voice, they're able to command greater attention and to further assert their dominance, even when what they're saying doesn't really make much sense.
W: And retaining their power and prestige is their priority.
M: It's what makes the most sense to a lot of them.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. They can hit fastballs coming at them at nearly 100 miles an hour, and leap and hang in the air, seemingly defying gravity. They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts, and their names and faces appear on everything from running shoes to advertising boards.
Athletes who are champions also show qualities such as perseverance, dedication, and the ability to keep their cool under pressure. Many show those same qualities off the playing field, too. Stories about superstar athletes teach us about working hard and believing in ourselves and then being passionate about what we do. Although it's usually bad behavior that gets an athlete a spot on the six o'clock news, many high-profile players work hard to be positive role models to children. They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school.
Still, even the greatest champions have flaws. Just because an athlete has the perfect golf swing doesn't mean he is the perfect parent, friend or spokesperson. They also make mistakes. Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. When a sports star gets in trouble with the law, or does something wrong in their private life, fans are often left disappointed. Before he died, baseball star Mickey Mantle, who was plagued with alcohol problems, told young ballplayers and the fans who admired him "to play like me, don't be like me."

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive. Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur. While most brides tend to accept this as fact, one Canadian woman, who is only known as Susan, attempted to avoid all wedding costs. She did this by asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding. It went about as well as you'd expect. Susan is causing quite the debate online after posting a bizarre Facebook complaint about her now-cancelled wedding.
Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows. Since their guests refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold. In her long explanation filled with cursing and swearing, the bride accused her friends and family of ruining her marriage and her life. She stated that each guest would only need to pay $1,500 while she sacrificed everything for the day. Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests. But Susan ignored her. Not surprisingly, only eight people responded positively to the wedding invitations and money requests.
Realizing they would not be able to afford their dream wedding, Susan's future husband suggested getting married in Las Vegas. The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking. It seems her dream wedding has now become a nightmare.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods. Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities. This study of over 1.6 million people revealed that 22 degrees Celsius is the perfect air temperature to live in. A city with an average annual temperature closer to 22 tends to have a population who are more agreeable, conscientious, emotionally stable, and outgoing. It is the least taxing temperature for the body to regulate its own temperature.
The study was observational and didn't show cause and effect, but the scientists behind it theorized that better weather leads people to leave their home more often. This, in turn, leads to more social interaction, which encourages them to develop a friendlier and socially more acceptable personality. Warmer climates also make people feel more positive in general. They tend to be more agreeable and conscientious.
The findings might help explain why colder and warmer countries tend to produce people with different personalities. Roughly speaking, about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes, the other 60% by their environment. It was already well-known that personality traits vary across geographic regions. Scientists also knew that these geographic personality traits are associated with a broad range of consequential outcomes. These outcomes include economic activity, for example, entrepreneurial start-up rates, and also crime rates, health behaviors, and health outcomes.
And it is well established that personality traits differ between countries. The research team speculated the two might be linked. To test this, they gave online personality tests to 5,587 Chinese students and 1.66 million Americans. They then compared the results with the average annual temperature where they grew up. The tests measured personality along five well-studied characteristics. The five were agreeability, conscientiousness, emotional stability, outgoingness, and openness to new experiences. In both groups, the researchers found the closer a town's average annual temperature was to 22 degrees, the more its population exhibited those personality characteristics.
However, the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied, which suggests that though temperature plays a role, it does not play a dominant role. The effects are fairly weak. It's unlikely to lead to many arguments over the temperature setting of the office air conditioner.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Today, we are talking about loneliness. Loneliness and social isolation are growing public health concerns for people of all ages in the United States, from adolescence to the elderly. Public health experts are worried because loneliness seems to be on the rise, and studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions that threaten health and longevity.
The problem of loneliness may be even greater than we thought. A new national poll found that about a third of older Americans are lonely, and almost as many seniors feel isolated. This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens. That's because it can impair older adults' memory and damage their physical and mental health. Chronic loneliness even impacts the life expectancy of seniors, increasing their risk of early mortality.
Let's take a closer look at that poll now. More than a third of seniors in the poll said they felt lonely at least some of the time, and 27% said they sometimes or often felt isolated. This reflects how much time the seniors spent with others. Almost 30% said they socialized with friends, family or neighbors once a week or less. Women were more likely than men to report loneliness.
But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. But researchers are still trying to determine the best way to do so. Why is that? Resolving the problem of loneliness among seniors often isn't as simple as getting them together with others or moving them in with their children. In fact, the poll found that seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely than those who didn't. This may be because loneliness refers to the discrepancy between actual and desired relationships. So it's possible that someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition, while someone in a house full of busy people does.
How can we solve the problem? Well, the researchers assert that it's important to address each person's underlying cause of loneliness, whether it's the death of a spouse, medical problems, or social expectations that haven't been fulfilled. It's noteworthy that there is one general recommendation. While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week. Depending on the person, that could mean volunteering, seeing an old friend or something else.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Hello, I'm co-founder of the popular female travel community We Are Travel Girls. We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world. We promote women's blogs; we host meetings and events and are getting ready to launch our Travel With Us trips in Bali, Japan and Malawi.
Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10-year career in finance in London, where I advised private clients on their investments. Having always had a huge love for travel, I finally took the leap and left finance to pursue my dream of starting a travel company.
For as long as I can remember, I wanted to be a travel writer. Before blogs existed and everything we read was online, I would go to travel writing seminars by writers who were published in travel magazines. I was desperate to write for one of those magazines, but didn't know how to break into that industry. After university, I ended up working in finance, but always had a desire to travel and write about it.
In 2015, I was looking at ways to leave finance, and my best friend Vanessa, who grew up on a ranch on the Central Coast of California, suggested starting a blog. But when we started creating it, we realized that was the same thing every girl was doing. So we turned our attention to creating a community among these women. This led us to start We Are Travel Girls, which has now grown into a community of over 200,000 followers.
To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry. There are a lot of travel writers now and it can be hard to stand out from the crowd, which is really why we started We Are Travel Girls. Be prepared to work hard if you want to turn it into a full-time business, and try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience. The size of your audience doesn't necessarily need to be huge, but you want them to be engaged. If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off.

questions.prompt: Where does the conversation most probably take place?
options: In a restaurant.
In a kitchen.
In a food store.
In a supermarket.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where does the conversation most probably take place? 

 【翻译】 对话最可能发生在哪里? 
 A)  在餐馆里。 
 B)  在厨房里。 
 C)  在食品店里。 
 D)  在超市里。 

 【答案】 A （推断题） In a restaurant. 
 【定位】 P2 But one of my close friends ate here last week. She's a vegetarian. She told me that there were a lot of options for her, and they offered alternative dishes. 
 不过我一个好朋友上周在这儿吃过。她是素食者。她跟我说这里给她的选择很多，还提供替代菜品。 

 【信号】 menu、ate here、offered dishes 等餐厅标志词 。环境标志词成串出现：第1段 I've been wanting to try this place、第2段 the menu 与 they offered alternative dishes、第10段 What are you going to have?——「菜单、上菜、点什么」只可能发生在餐厅，多个标志词共同锁定地点。 

 【替换】 the menu ↔ In a restaurant. 有菜单、有人上菜的场所即餐厅 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 kitchen（厨房）借的是 dishes、menu 引发的「跟做饭有关」联想，但全程是别人给两人上菜、问他们点什么，没人在自己下厨，地点不是厨房。  借用原文：they offered alternative dishes 

 C) 原词陷阱 food store（食品店）只是蹭了满篇的食物话题，可对话里是坐下来看菜单、被问点什么，没有任何挑选购买商品的情节，与食品店不符。 
 D) 原词陷阱 supermarket（超市）与 food store 错法相同，只因话题是吃就被列进来，但录音里 What are you going to have? 是点餐、不是购物，排除。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman?
options: She eats meat occasionally.
She enjoys cheeseburgers.
She is allergic to seafood.
She is a partial vegetarian.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the woman? 

 【翻译】 关于这位女士我们了解到什么? 
 A)  她偶尔吃肉。 
 B)  她喜欢吃芝士汉堡。 
 C)  她对海鲜过敏。 
 D)  她是一位部分素食者。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） She is a partial vegetarian. 
 【定位】 P4 Well, not entirely. I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs. 
 嗯，不完全是。我完全不吃肉，但吃鱼、海鲜或蛋是没问题的。 

 【信号】 被问者应答 + not entirely 让步 + but 转折 。男士问 you're not vegetarian, are you?，女士的应答即落点；她先说 not entirely（不完全是），再用 but 把「不吃肉」和「吃鱼蛋」对接——这种「部分是、不完全是」正是 partial vegetarian 的定义。 

 【替换】 I don't eat meat at all, but I don't have a problem eating fish, seafood or eggs ↔ She is a partial vegetarian. 「不吃肉但吃鱼蛋」概括为「部分素食者」 
 not entirely ↔ partial vegetarian 「不完全是」对应「部分」 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 She eats meat occasionally.（偶尔吃肉）与原文 I don't eat meat at all（完全不吃肉）正好相反，把「一点都不吃」反成了「偶尔吃」。  借用原文：I don't eat meat at all 

 B) 张冠李戴 She enjoys cheeseburgers. 盗用了男士那句 bacon cheeseburgers，但说舍不得汉堡的是男士、不是女士，把男方的话安到了女方头上。  借用原文：bacon cheeseburgers 

 C) 原词陷阱 She is allergic to seafood. 盗用了 seafood 一词，但原文是她「吃海鲜没问题」，根本没提过敏，allergic 系凭空捏造且与事实相反。  借用原文：eating fish, seafood or eggs

questions.prompt: What would be a difficult thing to do according to the woman?
options: Dealing with one's colleagues.
Changing one's eating habit.
Following the same diet for years.
Keeping awake at morning meetings.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What would be a difficult thing to do according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据这位女士的说法,什么事情会比较难做到? 
 A)  与同事打交道。 
 B)  改变饮食习惯。 
 C)  多年保持同样的饮食。 
 D)  在早晨会议上保持清醒。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Changing one's eating habit. 
 【定位】 P6 I bet it would be hard though, giving up something you're accustomed to eating. 
 不过我敢说，要放弃一样你习惯了的吃食，是会很难的。 

 【信号】 评价词 hard 直接修饰 giving up… eating 。it would be hard 里的 hard（难）直接评价后面的 giving up something you're accustomed to eating——「放弃一样你已习惯吃的东西」，评价词紧贴的那件事就是答案，正是「改变饮食习惯」。 

 【替换】 giving up something you're accustomed to eating ↔ Changing one's eating habit. 「放弃习惯吃的东西」=「改变饮食习惯」 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Dealing with one's colleagues. 盗用了 deal with me 旁边的 colleagues，但原文是「戒咖啡后同事得忍受我很难受」，难的是戒咖啡这件事，不是「处理同事」。  借用原文：deal with me at morning meetings 

 C) 原词陷阱 Following the same diet for years. 蹭了 My parents followed the same diet，可那是在讲她从小随父母吃同样的饭、并不觉得难，不是被评为「难做」的事。  借用原文：My parents followed the same diet 

 D) 原词陷阱 Keeping awake at morning meetings. 借用了 morning meetings，但原文只说戒咖啡让她早会上状态差、同事难受，从没说「在早会保持清醒」是难事，系拼凑原词。  借用原文：morning meetings

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her parents?
options: They enjoy perfect health.
They are both animal lovers.
They only eat organic food.
They are cutting back on coffee.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about her parents? 

 【翻译】 这位女士关于她父母说了什么? 
 A)  他们身体非常健康。 
 B)  他们都是动物爱好者。 
 C)  他们只吃有机食品。 
 D)  他们正在减少咖啡摄入量。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They enjoy perfect health. 
 【定位】 P8 Both are in their 70s now, but eat organic as often as possible and take part in regular physical exercise. Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick. 
 他们俩现在都七十多岁了，但尽量常吃有机食品，也定期参加体育锻炼。两人都没有任何健康问题，也几乎从不生病。 

 【信号】 强否定 Neither…any + hardly ever 收束健康结论 。落点在 Neither of them has any health problems 与 they hardly ever get sick——双重否定 + hardly ever 把父母身体状况推到「完全没病、几乎不生病」的极佳状态，这是对父母的总体定论。 

 【替换】 Neither of them has any health problems, and they hardly ever get sick ↔ They enjoy perfect health. 「都没病、几乎不生病」=「身体极佳」 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 They are both animal lovers. 借了 animal preservation 一词，但原文说父母 not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts（对动物保护既不热心也不懂），与「都是爱动物者」相反。  借用原文：not terribly active or knowledgeable about animal preservation efforts 

 C) 偷换概念 They only eat organic food. 盗用 eat organic，却把原文的 as often as possible（尽量常吃）偷改成 only（只吃），范围被绝对化，不符。  借用原文：eat organic as often as possible 

 D) 张冠李戴 They are cutting back on coffee. 盗用了 cutting back on coffee，但戒咖啡的是女士自己（I tried cutting back on coffee），父母从未减咖啡，把女士的事安到了父母身上。  借用原文：I tried cutting back on coffee

questions.prompt: What was the manager's reason for giving little praise for the man's performance?
options: The man got a poor evaluation from his colleagues.
The man made little contribution to the company.
The man paid attention to trivial things.
The man had an attitude problem.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the manager's reason for giving little praise for the man's performance? 

 【翻译】 经理对这名男士的工作表现几乎不予赞扬的原因是什么? 
 A)  这名男士从同事那里得到了较差的评价。 
 B)  这名男士对公司贡献甚微。 
 C)  这名男士关注琐碎的事情。 
 D)  这名男士有态度问题。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The man had an attitude problem. 
 【定位】 P2 he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem. 
 他直截了当地告诉我，我有态度问题。 

 【信号】 被问者复述经理原话的直接引述句 。女士问考评结果后，男士应答里 he bluntly told me that I had an attitude problem 是对经理原话的直接转述，'他告诉我……'这种引述就是答案信号——经理给出的原因被原原本本复述在这句里。 

 【替换】 I had an attitude problem ↔ The man had an attitude problem. 原话第一人称 I，选项换成第三人称 The man，意思不变 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 原文差评出自男士的 manager(见 your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager)，A 却说 a poor evaluation from his colleagues'来自同事'，张冠李戴改了评价来源，故错。  借用原文：your annual performance evaluation meeting with your manager 

 B) 未提及 经理给的理由是态度问题，全程没说男士 made little contribution to the company'贡献少'，这是凭'表扬少'常识脑补出的原因，原文无据。 
 C) 原词陷阱 原文经理说 it's the little things I do and say，C 的 paid attention to trivial things 用 trivial(琐碎)勾住这个 little things，听着像。但原文 little things 指'惹经理不快的琐碎言行(即态度的体现)'，不是说男士'只关注琐事'，含义被偷换。  借用原文：it's the little things I do and say

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about some managers?
options: They make unhelpful decisions for solving problems.
They favor some employees' suggestions over others.
They use manipulative language to mask their irrational choices.
They reject employees' reasonable arguments for work efficiency.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about some managers? 

 【翻译】 女士对一些管理者有什么看法? 
 A)  他们在解决问题时做出无益的决定。 
 B)  他们偏爱某些员工的建议而非其他人的建议。 
 C)  他们使用操纵性语言来掩盖其不理性的选择。 
 D)  他们拒绝员工关于提高工作效率的合理论证。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They use manipulative language to mask their irrational choices. 
 【定位】 P5 Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices they have made. 
 有些经理确实会采用操控性的语言，来掩饰他们做出的那些不合理的选择。 

 【信号】 女士发言中直接评价经理的核心陈述句 。女士这段以 Some managers really adopt manipulative language to disguise the unreasonable choices 直陈对经理的判断，主语 Some managers、动词 adopt…to disguise 把'手段+目的'说全，是承载答案的评价句。 

 【替换】 adopt manipulative language ↔ use manipulative language adopt 换成 use，同义动词替换 
 disguise the unreasonable choices ↔ mask their irrational choices disguise→mask、unreasonable→irrational 双重同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 原文批评的是经理'用话术掩盖不合理决定'，重点在'掩盖'这个语言行为；A 的 make unhelpful decisions for solving problems 只截取'决定不好'一层，丢了'操控语言'的核心，且 unhelpful 与原文 unreasonable 侧重不同，未答到点上。  借用原文：disguise the unreasonable choices they have made 

 B) 未提及 原文没说经理 favor some employees' suggestions over others'偏心采纳某些建议'，这是凭'经理不公'的印象自造的指控，原文无对应句。 
 D) 原词陷阱 原文紧接的下一句是 They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues'他们不用理性论证去解决问题'，D 的 reject employees' reasonable arguments for work efficiency 盗用 rational/arguments 这两个原词，并自添 for work efficiency(为了效率)的动机，原文既没说'否决员工合理论点'，更没提'效率'，原词在意思被改向。  借用原文：They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues of conflict

questions.prompt: According to the woman, what do some managers think of honesty?
options: It is a must for rational judgment.
It is more of a sin than a virtue.
It is a good quality in the workplace.
It is more important now than ever.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the woman, what do some managers think of honesty? 

 【翻译】 根据女士的说法,一些管理者如何看待诚实? 
 A)  诚实是理性判断的必要条件。 
 B)  诚实更像是一种罪过而非美德。 
 C)  诚实是职场中的一种良好品质。 
 D)  诚实现在比以往任何时候都更重要。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） It is more of a sin than a virtue. 
 【定位】 P7 Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue, since it made people feel uncomfortable. 
 诚实被认为更像是一种罪过而非美德，因为它让人感到不舒服。 

 【信号】 评价动词 deemed 引出的定性，是态度落点 。女士用 Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue，deemed(被认为是)后面跟的 a sin(罪)就是这些经理对诚实的定性，评价性动词后的内容正是态度题答案信号。 

 【替换】 more of a sin than a virtue ↔ more of a sin than a virtue 此项罕见地原句照搬，反成正确项 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 原文把诚实判为 more of a sin than a virtue'更像罪'，是负面；A 的 It is a must for rational judgment'理性判断的必需品'是正面拔高，极性与原文相反。  借用原文：Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue 

 C) 与原文相反 C 的 It is a good quality in the workplace'职场好品质'是正面评价，而原文这些经理把诚实看作 a sin(负面)，褒贬相反；workplace 虽是全篇高频词，但拿它包装的却是与原意相反的正面判断。  借用原文：Honesty was deemed to be more of a sin than a virtue 

 D) 未提及 原文谈的是诚实被看作罪/还是美德，从没说它 more important now than ever'现在比过去更重要'，时间今昔的维度原文完全没出现。

questions.prompt: What does the woman think is the priority of many managers?
options: Smoothing relationships in the workplace.
Making rational and productive decisions.
Focusing on employees career growth.
Preserving their power and prestige.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman think is the priority of many managers? 

 【翻译】 女士认为许多管理者的首要任务是什么? 
 A)  协调职场中的关系。 
 B)  做出理性且富有成效的决定。 
 C)  关注员工的职业发展。 
 D)  维护他们的权力和威望。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Preserving their power and prestige. 
 【定位】 P9 And retaining their power and prestige is their priority. 
 而且，保住他们的权力和威望，才是他们的首要之务。 

 【信号】 对话收尾处带 priority 的结论句 。临近结束，女士用 And retaining their power and prestige is their priority 直接点出 priority，以 And 收束全段批评、给出结论，正是答案信号——对话的总结判断落在这句。 

 【替换】 retaining their power and prestige ↔ Preserving their power and prestige. retaining 换成 preserving，同义动词替换 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 原文说经理首要是保权保威，从没说他们以 Smoothing relationships in the workplace'维系职场关系'为先，这是凭好印象自造的目标，原文无对应。 
 B) 原词陷阱 原文多处用到 rational(如 They don't use the rational power of arguments)，B 的 Making rational and productive decisions'做理性高效决定'正是拿这个高频词设套；但全篇批评经理不理性、靠话术保权，把'理性决策'当成他们的首要恰恰相反。  借用原文：They don't use the rational power of arguments to resolve issues 

 C) 未提及 原文通篇批评经理只顾自己权威，绝无说他们以 Focusing on employees career growth'员工职业成长'为先，这与结论句的'保权'完全背离，原文无据。

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say athletes are often viewed as heroes?
options: They show genius which defies description.
They accomplish feats many of us cannot.
They create very high commercial value.
They bring great honor to their country.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker say athletes are often viewed as heroes? 

 【翻译】 为什么说话者说运动员常被视为英雄？ 
 A)  他们展现了难以言表的天赋。 
 B)  他们完成了我们许多人无法做到的壮举。 
 C)  他们创造了非常高的商业价值。 
 D)  他们为国家带来巨大荣誉。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They accomplish feats many of us cannot. 
 【定位】 P1 Athletes are seen as heroes because they can do things that most of us can't do. 
 运动员被视为英雄，是因为他们能做到我们多数人做不到的事。 

 【信号】 because 后紧跟原因 。答案信号是因果连词 because，它后面 they can do things that most of us can't do 正是录音给出的理由，因果词后那一句就是答案落点。 

 【替换】 do things that most of us can't do ↔ accomplish feats many of us cannot 同义改写：do things=accomplish feats 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They show genius which defies description. 的天赋/无法描述在录音里没有对应表述；录音说的是做到常人做不到的事，并未夸张到天才到无法形容，属拔高式编造。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They create very high commercial value. 借了录音里 They get paid millions of dollars 和广告板出现这层商业画面来诱选，但那是顺带描述、并非说话人给出的成为英雄的原因；题问 Why are they heroes，答案是能力而非商业价值，听到钱就选会中招。  借用原文：They get paid millions of dollars for their efforts 

 D) 未提及 They bring great honor to their country. 的 country/为国争光在整段录音里没出现过，是听力惯用的拔高型干扰，第一步预读时已提醒要警惕 country 是否真被提到。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say many high-profile players do?
options: They take part in kids' extra-curricular activities.
They work in spare time to teach children sports.
They try to be positive role models to children.
They serve as spokespersons for luxury goods.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say many high-profile players do? 

 【翻译】 说话者说许多知名球员会做什么？ 
 A)  他们参加孩子们的课外活动。 
 B)  他们利用业余时间教孩子们体育运动。 
 C)  他们努力成为孩子们的积极榜样。 
 D)  他们担任奢侈品的代言人。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They try to be positive role models to children. 
 【定位】 P2 They raise money for charities and act as mentors, talking to student groups and volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school. 
 他们为慈善募款、担任导师，与学生群体交流，并把时间投入到帮助孩子远离毒品、留在学校的项目中。 

 【信号】 主语承接后的行为列举 。答案句承接上句 many high-profile players work hard to be positive role models to children，紧接着用 volunteering their time to programs that help children keep off drugs and stay in school 具体列举其作为，行为列举处即题问的落点。 

 【替换】 help children keep off drugs and stay in school ↔ Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems keep off=keep away from 同义 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They take part in kids' extra-curricular activities. 借录音里频繁出现的 children/student groups 这层与孩子相关的画面诱选，但录音说的是 talking to student groups、volunteering，并非 take part in 课外活动，动作对不上。  借用原文：talking to student groups 

 B) 未提及 They work in spare time to teach children sports. 利用录音里 children 一词及对孩子的帮助来诱选，但录音从未说他们利用业余时间教孩子体育，teach ... sports 与 spare time 都是录音没有的添加。  借用原文：help children keep off drugs and stay in school 

 D) 与原文相反 They serve as spokespersons for luxury goods. 把这群正面榜样说成代言奢侈品，方向与录音里 work hard to be positive role models to children 的公益形象相反，且 luxury goods 录音未提。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say can be difficult?
options: Separating an athlete's professional life from their personal life.
Preventing certain athletes from getting in trouble with the law.
Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems.
Being super sports stars without appearing arrogant.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say can be difficult? 

 【翻译】 说话者说什么可能很困难？ 
 A)  将运动员的职业生活与个人生活分开。 
 B)  防止某些运动员触犯法律。 
 C)  让运动员远离毒品或酒精问题。 
 D)  成为超级体育明星而不显得傲慢。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Separating an athlete's professional life from their personal life. 
 【定位】 P3 Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives can be tough. 
 把运动员的职业生活与私人生活分开，可能很难。 

 【信号】 tough 这一难易判断词 。答案信号是 can be tough 里的 tough，它正是题干 difficult 的同义词，与它搭配的 Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives 即题问的那件难事。 

 【替换】 Separating an athlete's professional and personal lives ↔ Separating an athlete's professional life from their personal life 几乎原句，仅句式微调 
 can be tough ↔ can be difficult tough=difficult 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Preventing certain athletes from getting in trouble with the law. 直接搬录音里 gets in trouble with the law 的原话诱选，但录音是把触犯法律当作运动员会犯错的举例，并没说防止其触法是件难事，问的难事是分开两种生活。  借用原文：When a sports star gets in trouble with the law 

 C) 原词陷阱 Keeping athletes away from drug or alcohol problems. 借录音 plagued with alcohol problems 的醒目词诱选，但那是 Mickey Mantle 个人遭遇的举例，录音没把远离毒品酒精说成困难，与 tough 搭配的并非此事。  借用原文：Mickey Mantle, who was plagued with alcohol problems 

 D) 未提及 Being super sports stars without appearing arrogant. 的不显傲慢在录音里没有任何对应，arrogant 一词及相关意思整段未出现，属凭空编造的难处。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about weddings?
options: They always cost more than expected.
They are joyous and exciting occasions.
They should be paid up by the attendees.
They are dreams coming true to the brides.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about weddings? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于婚礼说了什么? 
 A)  婚礼的花费总是超出预期。 
 B)  婚礼是欢乐和激动人心的场合。 
 C)  婚礼应该由参加者付费。 
 D)  婚礼是新娘梦想成真的时刻。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They always cost more than expected. 
 【定位】 P1 We don't need to tell you that weddings can get expensive. Even with the most meticulous budgeting, a few unexpected costs are bound to occur. 
 不用我们说你也知道，婚礼会变得很烧钱。哪怕预算做得再精细，也难免冒出一些意料之外的开销。 

 【信号】 开篇总起句直接定调 。篇章第一句 weddings can get expensive 就是开门见山的总起，紧接着 a few unexpected costs are bound to occur 进一步坐实"花费会超出预料"。开头总起句是篇章题最常见的答案信号，听到第一句定性就该锁定。 

 【替换】 a few unexpected costs are bound to occur ↔ cost more than expected unexpected costs = cost more than expected 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 They are joyous and exciting occasions.（欢乐激动的场合）听起来像婚礼常识，很诱人，但说话人开篇的定性是"烧钱、超预算"，全篇也是讲婚礼黄掉的糟心事，根本没说婚礼欢乐。这是用生活常识代替原文的典型坑。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They should be paid up by the attendees.（该由出席者付费）盗用了原文 asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding 里的 pay up、attend——但那是 Susan 一个人的荒唐做法，不是 speaker 对"婚礼"的普遍看法。听到 pay up 就选，正中原词陷阱。  借用原文：asking her friends and family to pay up to attend her wedding 

 D) 原词陷阱 They are dreams coming true to the brides. 借用了原文反复出现的 dream wedding、brides，听着顺耳。但原文的 dream wedding 是讽刺 Susan 那场最终变 nightmare 的婚礼，绝非说"婚礼是新娘美梦成真"。这是把后文的反讽细节误当成开篇定性。  借用原文：the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the wedding of the Canadian woman Susan?
options: It cost $60,000.
It was cancelled.
It had eight guests only.
It was held in Las Vegas.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the wedding of the Canadian woman Susan? 

 【翻译】 关于加拿大女性Susan的婚礼,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  婚礼花费了60000美元。 
 B)  婚礼被取消了。 
 C)  婚礼只有八位宾客。 
 D)  婚礼在Las Vegas举行。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It was cancelled. 
 【定位】 P2 Yes, the couple called off the wedding just days before their wedding vows. Since their guests refused to pay the $1,500 attendance fee, the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold. 
 是的，这对新人在交换结婚誓言前几天取消了婚礼。由于宾客拒付 1500 美元的出席费，这场 6 万美元的梦想婚礼被永久搁置了。 

 【信号】 结局动词 called off / put on permanent hold 。答案落在表"取消"的动作上：the couple called off the wedding 与 put on permanent hold 直接交代了婚礼的最终结局。问"这场婚礼怎么了"，结局性动词就是定位信号，盖过其中的数字干扰。 

 【替换】 the couple called off the wedding ↔ It was cancelled. called off = was cancelled 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It cost $60,000. 里的 6 万美元录音确实念到了——the $60,000 dream wedding——但原文是说这场"标价 6 万的梦想婚礼被搁置"，并不是说它"真的花掉了 6 万"（婚礼根本没办成）。听到 $60,000 就选，正中数字原词陷阱。  借用原文：the $60,000 dream wedding was put on permanent hold 

 C) 原词陷阱 It had eight guests only. 借了原文 only eight people responded positively 里的 eight。但那"八个人"是"积极回应邀请和付费要求的人数"，而婚礼根本取消了、压根没有出席的宾客。把"回应的八人"偷换成"到场八位宾客"，是细节偷换。  借用原文：only eight people responded positively to the wedding invitations and money requests 

 D) 原词陷阱 It was held in Las Vegas. 盗用了原文地名 getting married in Las Vegas。但拉斯维加斯只是未婚夫"提议"的地点，且 Susan 当场否决了，婚礼根本没在那办、也没办成。地名被搬到错误的事实上，是张冠李戴式原词陷阱。  借用原文：Susan's future husband suggested getting married in Las Vegas

questions.prompt: What did Susan's maid of honor advise her to do?
options: Postpone her wedding.
Ask her friends for help.
Keep to her budget.
Invite more guests.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Susan's maid of honor advise her to do? 

 【翻译】 Susan的伴娘建议她做什么? 
 A)  推迟她的婚礼。 
 B)  向她的朋友寻求帮助。 
 C)  遵守她的预算。 
 D)  邀请更多宾客。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Keep to her budget. 
 【定位】 P2 Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget, as she was asking too much from her guests. 
 她的伴娘劝她守住预算，因为她对宾客的要求太过分了。 

 【信号】 建议信号 told her to 。Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget 中的 told her to 就是"建议"信号，信号后紧跟的动作 stick to the budget 即答案所在。听建议题，认准 told sb to / advised 这类信号，落点就在其后的动词短语。 

 【替换】 stick to the budget ↔ Keep to her budget stick to = keep to 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Postpone her wedding. 听着合理（婚礼出问题了，推迟很常见），但伴娘说的是守预算，从没提推迟。婚礼最后是被取消（called off）而非推迟，考生易把"取消"的印象误当成伴娘建议"推迟"。 
 B) 与原文相反 Ask her friends for help. 恰恰反了：原文里 Susan 正是因为 asking too much from her guests（向宾客 / 朋友要太多）才闹崩，伴娘是劝她"别再这么要了、守预算"，而非劝她"找朋友帮忙"。方向完全相反。  借用原文：she was asking too much from her guests 

 D) 与原文相反 Invite more guests. 与伴娘的本意相悖。伴娘嫌 Susan 对宾客要求太多、要她收着点（守预算），怎会让她再多邀客人？这是把建议方向取反的干扰项。  借用原文：Her maid of honor told her to stick to the budget

questions.prompt: How did Susan respond to her future husband's suggestion?
options: She called it romantic.
She welcomed it with open arms.
She said she would think about it.
She rejected it flatly.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did Susan respond to her future husband's suggestion? 

 【翻译】 Susan如何回应她未婚夫的建议? 
 A)  她称这个建议很浪漫。 
 B)  她张开双臂欢迎这个建议。 
 C)  她说她会考虑一下。 
 D)  她断然拒绝了。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） She rejected it flatly. 
 【定位】 P3 The bride quickly shut down the idea, saying she did not want a wedding of gambling and heavy drinking. 
 新娘很快否决了这个主意，说她不想要一场满是赌博和酗酒的婚礼。 

 【信号】 强否定动作 shut down + 理由 。The bride quickly shut down the idea 里 shut down（直接否决）加上副词 quickly，语气强烈而干脆；后面 she did not want 的否定理由再次坐实拒绝。态度题就抓这种强否定动作 + 否定理由作为信号。 

 【替换】 quickly shut down the idea ↔ rejected it flatly quickly shut down = rejected flatly 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 She called it romantic.（说它浪漫）是正面反应，与原文 shut down the idea 的干脆否决完全相反。原文里浪漫一词根本没出现，是凭"婚礼"联想出的诱选。  借用原文：The bride quickly shut down the idea 

 B) 与原文相反 She welcomed it with open arms.（张开双臂欢迎）是强烈接受，恰与 Susan 的强烈拒绝相对。这是把态度光谱拨到了相反一端的干扰。  借用原文：quickly shut down the idea 

 C) 偷换概念 She said she would think about it.（说她会考虑）是夹在接受与拒绝之间的中间态度，最像"温和版"答案。但原文是 quickly shut down——又快又决绝，没有任何"再想想"的余地。把强否定弱化成"考虑"，是程度偷改。  借用原文：The bride quickly shut down the idea

questions.prompt: What has a new study revealed about temperature?
options: It determines people's moods.
It can impact people's wellbeing.
It is closely related to people's emotions.
It can influence people's personalities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has a new study revealed about temperature? 

 【翻译】 一项新研究揭示了关于温度的什么信息? 
 A)  它决定人们的心情。 
 B)  它会影响人们的幸福感。 
 C)  它与人们的情绪密切相关。 
 D)  它会影响人们的性格。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It can influence people's personalities. 
 【定位】 P1 Now, a new study has provided evidence that temperature can influence people's personalities. 
 如今，一项新研究提供了证据，表明温度能够影响人的性格。 

 【信号】 Now 引出新结论 。前一句说"天气影响情绪"早已是定论，紧接 Now, a new study has provided evidence 用 "Now"（如今）把新旧对照开来——"Now+新研究"正是答案信号，新研究的新发现就在这句，落点是 temperature can influence people's personalities。 

 【替换】 temperature can influence people's personalities ↔ It can influence people's personalities. 近乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A"决定人的情绪 moods"盗用了原文 weather changes can affect people's moods 里的 moods，但那是"早已确立的旧定论"、且用的是 affect（影响）不是 determine（决定），并非"新研究的发现"，听到 moods 就选会掉进时间错位的坑。  借用原文：weather changes can affect people's moods 

 B) 未提及 B 说温度"影响人的福祉 wellbeing"，可原文新研究讲的是影响"personalities 性格"，从没出现 wellbeing 这层；属凭"听着合理"硬填，原文无据。 
 C) 答非所问 C"与情绪密切相关 closely related to emotions"对应的是 weather changes can affect people's moods 那条"早已确立"的旧知识，不是"new study revealed"的新发现；既错在时间（旧非新），"closely"也夸大了原文 affect 的程度。  借用原文：It has long been scientifically established that weather changes can affect people's moods.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about warmer climates?
options: They make people more reproductive.
They increase people's life expectancy.
They tend to produce positive feelings.
They may alter people's genes gradually.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about warmer climates? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于较温暖的气候说了什么? 
 A)  它们使人们更具生殖能力。 
 B)  它们延长人们的预期寿命。 
 C)  它们往往会产生积极的情绪。 
 D)  它们可能会逐渐改变人们的基因。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They tend to produce positive feelings. 
 【定位】 P2 Warmer climates also make people feel more positive in general. 
 温暖的气候总体上还会让人感觉更积极。 

 【信号】 主语直点 warmer climates 。这句主语就是题干路标词 Warmer climates，谓语 "make people feel more positive" 正面回答"温暖气候使人怎样"，是直接应答式的答案句，无需转折也无需推断。 

 【替换】 make people feel more positive in general ↔ They tend to produce positive feelings. 使人感觉积极=产生积极感受 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A"使人更能生育 reproductive"原文从未提及生育这一层，是凭"暖→繁衍"的常识硬推，无原文依据。 
 B) 未提及 B"延长寿命 life expectancy"听着像健康类结论，但原文谈温暖气候只说让人更积极、更友善，从未涉及寿命；属合理却无据。 
 D) 张冠李戴 D"逐渐改变人的基因 genes"盗用了原文 about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes 里的 genes，但原文 genes 是讲"基因决定四成性格"，根本不是说"温暖气候改变基因"；把别处的词安到本题对象上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：about 40% of a person's personality is determined by their genes

questions.prompt: What did the online personality tests suggest?
options: The link between temperature and personality is fairly weak.
People share many personality traits despite their nationalities.
People in the same geographical area may differ in personality.
The Americans are apparently more outgoing than the Chinese.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the online personality tests suggest? 

 【翻译】 在线性格测试表明了什么? 
 A)  温度与性格之间的联系相当微弱。 
 B)  尽管国籍不同,人们有许多共同的性格特征。 
 C)  同一地理区域的人在性格上可能有所不同。 
 D)  美国人显然比中国人更外向。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The link between temperature and personality is fairly weak. 
 【定位】 P5 However, the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied, which suggests that though temperature plays a role, it does not play a dominant role. The effects are fairly weak. 
 然而，对中国组的研究结果比对所研究的美国人要强得多，这表明温度虽起作用，但并不起主导作用。其影响相当微弱。 

 【信号】 However 转折收束 。However 这个转折词把前文"温度越接近22度、性格越明显"的正面铺陈一收，转折后的 it does not play a dominant role 和 The effects are fairly weak 才是研究的真正定论——转折后才是落点，正是答案信号。 

 【替换】 The effects are fairly weak ↔ The link between temperature and personality is fairly weak. 影响弱=关联弱 
 it does not play a dominant role ↔ fairly weak 非主导=弱 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 B"人们尽管国籍不同却共享许多性格特质"，但原文 the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans 恰恰强调中美两组结果差别很大（中国组强得多），方向与"跨国籍相似"相反。  借用原文：the findings were much stronger for the Chinese group than the Americans studied 

 C) 答非所问 C"同一地理区域的人性格可能不同"借用了原文 personality traits vary across geographic regions 关于地区差异的说法，但那是第三段的背景旧知识，且讲的是"跨地区"差异，不是"测试 suggest"的结论；本题问 tests 说明了什么，答案在第五段的强弱定性，不在这里。  借用原文：personality traits vary across geographic regions 

 D) 原词陷阱 D"美国人显然比中国人更外向"盗用了原文测过的性格维度 outgoingness 和 Chinese/Americans 这些原词，但原文只说中国组的研究结果"更强"，从未比较两国谁更外向；是把听过的词拼成一个原文没下的结论。  借用原文：outgoingness

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker say the finding of a new national poll reveals a serious problem?
options: The number of older Americans living alone is on the rise.
Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular.
Correlations have been found between loneliness and ill health.
A growing number of US seniors face the risk of early mortality.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker say the finding of a new national poll reveals a serious problem? 

 【翻译】 为什么说话者说一项新的全国民意调查的发现揭示了一个严重的问题? 
 A)  独居的美国老年人数量正在上升。 
 B)  慢性孤独尤其对老年人造成伤害。 
 C)  孤独与健康不佳之间已被发现存在关联。 
 D)  越来越多的美国老年人面临早死的风险。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular. 
 【定位】 P2 This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens. 
 这是个严重的问题，因为研究显示长期的孤独对老年人尤其有害。 

 【信号】 原句直说 serious problem 加 as 因果 。录音里 This is a serious problem as research shows that chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens 用 a serious problem 直接呼应题干的 serious problem，再用 as（因为）引出原因——题干问 Why，答案就在这个 as 因果句里。 

 【替换】 chronic loneliness is particularly harmful to senior citizens ↔ Chronic loneliness does harm to senior citizens in particular 近义改写：harmful 换 does harm，particularly 换 in particular 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音第1段确实念过 loneliness seems to be on the rise，选项 The number of older Americans living alone is on the rise 顺手借了 on the rise 制造耳熟，但录音说的是孤独在上升，不是独居老人人数在上升，且这不是题干问的为何是严重问题，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：loneliness seems to be on the rise 

 C) 原词陷阱 第1段念过 correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions，选项 Correlations have been found between loneliness and ill health 借此造耳熟。但这是讲座开场的背景铺垫，题干问的是新民调揭示的严重问题，那条具体落在第2段的尤其伤害老人，C 答非所问。  借用原文：studies have long found correlations between loneliness and an assortment of medical conditions 

 D) 原词陷阱 第2段念过 increasing their risk of early mortality，选项 A growing number of US seniors face the risk of early mortality 借走 early mortality 与 risk。但录音说的是长期孤独提高了老人早亡风险，并没说越来越多老人面临早亡风险（人数增长），D 把风险升高偷换成人数增多，答非所问。  借用原文：increasing their risk of early mortality

questions.prompt: What is the good news the speaker talks about?
options: Medication is available for treating loneliness.
Loneliness rarely results from living alone.
Being busy helps fight loneliness.
Loneliness is probably reversible.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the good news the speaker talks about? 

 【翻译】 说话者谈到的好消息是什么? 
 A)  有药物可用于治疗孤独。 
 B)  孤独很少是独居造成的。 
 C)  忙碌有助于对抗孤独。 
 D)  孤独可能是可逆的。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Loneliness is probably reversible. 
 【定位】 P4 But there is good news. It looks like loneliness can be reversed. 
 但有个好消息。看起来孤独是可以被逆转的。 

 【信号】 转折 But 加提示词 good news 。录音 But there is good news 用转折 But 加题干同词 good news 双重提示，紧接的 loneliness can be reversed 就是好消息的内容——转折后/提示词后的那句才是真正落点。 

 【替换】 loneliness can be reversed ↔ Loneliness is probably reversible 词性转换：can be reversed 换 reversible 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音第5段提到 medical problems，选项 Medication is available for treating loneliness 借 medical 的耳熟造出有药可治。但录音只把 medical problems 列为孤独的诱因之一，从没说有药物能治疗孤独，属无中生有的原词陷阱。  借用原文：medical problems 

 B) 原词陷阱 第4段念过 someone who lives alone，选项 Loneliness rarely results from living alone 借 living alone 造耳熟。录音确实暗示独居未必孤独，但用 rarely（很少）把它说成了绝对判断，且这不是题干问的好消息那一句，答非所问。  借用原文：someone who lives alone doesn't meet that definition 

 C) 与原文相反 第4段念过 a house full of busy people，选项 Being busy helps fight loneliness 借 busy 造耳熟。可录音恰恰是说住在一屋子忙人中间的人反而可能孤独，busy 在原文是孤独的反例，C 把它反着用成忙碌能对抗孤独，与原文相反。  借用原文：someone in a house full of busy people does

questions.prompt: What is the key to solving the loneliness problem according to the speaker?
options: Living with one's children.
Meeting social expectations.
Meaningful social contact.
Timely medical intervention.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the key to solving the loneliness problem according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者的说法,解决孤独问题的关键是什么? 
 A)  与子女同住。 
 B)  满足社会期望。 
 C)  有意义的社交接触。 
 D)  及时的医疗干预。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Meaningful social contact. 
 【定位】 P5 While finding solutions for loneliness is highly personal, research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact at least once a week. 
 尽管为孤独寻找解决办法因人而异，但研究表明，最好的干预是那些每周至少有一次有意义社交接触的方式。 

 【信号】 推荐信号 research suggests the best 。录音 research suggests the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact 用 suggests 加 the best（最佳）双重推荐信号点名办法——题干问 the key，答案就在这个给推荐的句子里。 

 【替换】 meaningful social contact at least once a week ↔ Meaningful social contact 概括截取：选项是原句的核心保留 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 第4段念过 moving them in with their children，选项 Living with one's children 借 children 造耳熟。但录音明说和子女同住的老人反而更易孤独，把它当解决办法正好相反，是听到熟词就选的陷阱。  借用原文：seniors who lived with their children were more likely to report feeling lonely 

 B) 原词陷阱 第5段念过 social expectations that haven't been fulfilled，选项 Meeting social expectations 借 social expectations 造耳熟。但录音把它列为孤独的诱因之一，不是解决孤独的关键，B 答非所问。  借用原文：social expectations that haven't been fulfilled 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音念过 the best interventions 和第5段的 medical problems，选项 Timely medical intervention 拼合 medical 与 intervention 造耳熟。但录音说最佳 intervention 是有意义的社交接触，不是医疗干预；medical 在原文是诱因，D 张冠李戴。  借用原文：the best interventions are those that involve meaningful social contact

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the speaker before she created the community We Are Travel Girls?
options: She had a successful career in finance.
She wrote stories about women travelers.
She made regular trips to Asian countries.
She invested in several private companies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the speaker before she created the community We Are Travel Girls? 

 【翻译】 在创建 We Are Travel Girls 社区之前,我们对说话者有什么了解? 
 A)  她在金融领域有一份成功的职业。 
 B)  她撰写关于女性旅行者的故事。 
 C)  她定期前往亚洲国家旅行。 
 D)  她投资了几家私营公司。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She had a successful career in finance. 
 【定位】 P2 Before I started We Are Travel Girls, I had a successful 10-year career in finance in London, where I advised private clients on their investments. 
 在创办 We Are Travel Girls 之前，我在伦敦有过一段成功的、长达十年的金融职业生涯，在那里我为私人客户提供投资建议。 

 【信号】 时间信号 Before…对上题干 。答案句以 Before I started We Are Travel Girls 开头，与题干的 before she created the community 时间状语完全对应，这个『Before…』就是定位信号，它领出的那句正是讲她创办社区之前的身份。 

 【替换】 a successful 10-year career in finance ↔ a successful career in finance 几乎原句，只省去年限 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项 She wrote stories about women travelers. 盗用了录音第一段 We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world 里的 stories 与 women，但那是她现在做的社区业务、且是『收集发布』而非她个人『写』，题目问的是『创办社区之前』，时间和动作都对不上。  借用原文：We collect and publish stories from women traveling all over the world 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项 She made regular trips to Asian countries. 借了录音 launch our Travel With Us trips in Bali, Japan 里的 trips 和亚洲地名，但那是社区『正准备推出』的旅行项目（未来），不是她个人过去定期去亚洲，与题目问的『之前』不符。  借用原文：launch our Travel With Us trips in Bali, Japan and Malawi 

 D) 偷换概念 选项 She invested in several private companies. 盗用录音 I advised private clients on their investments 里的 private 和 invest，但原文是她『为私人客户提供投资建议』，主语和动作都被偷换成『她自己投资了几家私人公司』，意思已变。  借用原文：I advised private clients on their investments

questions.prompt: What did the speaker's friend suggest they do in 2015?
options: Buy a ranch.
Start a blog.
Travel round the world.
Set up a travel agency.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the speaker's friend suggest they do in 2015? 

 【翻译】 说话者的朋友在2015年建议她们做什么? 
 A)  购买一个牧场。 
 B)  创建一个博客。 
 C)  环游世界。 
 D)  成立一家旅行社。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Start a blog. 
 【定位】 P4 In 2015, I was looking at ways to leave finance, and my best friend Vanessa, who grew up on a ranch on the Central Coast of California, suggested starting a blog. 
 2015 年，我正在寻找离开金融业的办法，我最好的朋友 Vanessa——她在加州中央海岸的一个牧场长大——建议（我们）开一个博客。 

 【信号】 年份 In 2015 + suggested 双信号 。答案句同时出现题干两个关键信号：In 2015 对上题干的 in 2015，suggested starting a blog 里的 suggested 正对题干的 suggest，年份加建议动词双重锁定，这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 suggested starting a blog ↔ Start a blog 动词词形变化，意思不变 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Buy a ranch. 盗用录音 who grew up on a ranch on the Central Coast of California 里的 ranch，但 ranch 只是描述朋友在牧场长大的背景，没人提议『买牧场』，纯属听到 ranch 就选的陷阱。  借用原文：who grew up on a ranch on the Central Coast of California 

 C) 未提及 选项 Travel round the world. 借了本篇反复出现的 travel 主题氛围，但录音里朋友 2015 年的提议是开博客，从未提议『环游世界』，属未提及。 
 D) 偷换概念 选项 Set up a travel agency. 蹭了 travel 这个高频词，但录音里朋友提议的是 blog，后来她们转做 creating a community（社区），从没说要开『旅行社』，动作对不上。  借用原文：we turned our attention to creating a community among these women

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise people to do if they want to become travel writers?
options: Work hard to attract attention from publishers.
Gain support from travel advertising companies.
Try to find a full-time job in the travel business.
Create something unique to enter the industry.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker advise people to do if they want to become travel writers? 

 【翻译】 如果人们想成为旅行作家,说话者建议他们做什么? 
 A)  努力工作以吸引出版商的关注。 
 B)  获得旅游广告公司的支持。 
 C)  尝试在旅游行业找到一份全职工作。 
 D)  创造独特的东西以进入该行业。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Create something unique to enter the industry. 
 【定位】 P5 To anyone thinking about becoming a travel writer, I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry. 
 对任何想成为旅行作家的人，我建议他们首先去寻找一种独特的方式进入这个行业。 

 【信号】 建议信号 I would suggest 。答案句以 I would suggest they first try and look for a unique way to enter the industry 给出，I would suggest 是明确的建议信号词，对上题干的 advise，suggest 引出的内容就是她的忠告。 

 【替换】 look for a unique way to enter the industry ↔ Create something unique to enter the industry find a way 概括为 create something 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Work hard to attract attention from publishers. 借了录音另一句建议 Be prepared to work hard 里的 work hard，但她说努力是为了把它变成全职生意，根本没提『吸引出版商注意』，是把真实出现的 work hard 嫁接到没说过的目的上。  借用原文：Be prepared to work hard if you want to turn it into a full-time business 

 B) 与原文相反 选项 Gain support from travel advertising companies. 盗用录音 try not to rush to selling advertising spaces 里的 advertising，但原文是劝人『别急着卖广告位』，方向与『争取广告公司支持』相反，意思被反着用。  借用原文：try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience 

 C) 偷换概念 选项 Try to find a full-time job in the travel business. 蹭了录音 turn it into a full-time business 里的 full-time，但原文说的是把事业做成全职生意，不是叫人去找一份旅行业的全职工作，且这并非她对『如何入行』的核心建议。  借用原文：if you want to turn it into a full-time business

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's advice on winning a loyal audience?
options: Attracting sufficient investment.
Creating an exotic corporate culture.
Avoiding too much advertising early on.
Refraining from promoting similar products.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the speaker's advice on winning a loyal audience? 

 【翻译】 关于赢得忠实受众,说话者的建议是什么? 
 A)  吸引足够的投资。 
 B)  创建一种异国情调的企业文化。 
 C)  早期避免过多广告。 
 D)  避免推广类似产品。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Avoiding too much advertising early on. 
 【定位】 P5 Try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience. If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off. 
 在你培养起一批忠实受众之前，不要急着去卖广告位。如果你早期发太多推广，会让很多人反感离开。 

 【信号】 否定建议 try not to + early on 。答案句是 Try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience 和 If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off，try not to 这个否定建议信号配合 early on（早期），正是讲如何留住受众的关键句。 

 【替换】 try not to rush to selling advertising spaces before you have created a dedicated audience ↔ Avoiding too much advertising early on try not to 等于 avoiding，时机对应 early on 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Attracting sufficient investment. 里 investment 让人联想第二段她的金融/投资背景 advised private clients on their investments，但讲『赢得受众』的这段从未谈吸引投资，属拿别处话题词来干扰。  借用原文：I advised private clients on their investments 

 B) 未提及 选项 Creating an exotic corporate culture. 没有任何录音原句支撑，exotic corporate culture（异域企业文化）是凭旅行主题臆造出来的，与赢得受众的建议无关，属未提及。 
 D) 偷换概念 选项 Refraining from promoting similar products. 盗用录音 post too many promotions 里的 promotion，但原文劝的是『别在早期发太多推广』，问题在数量与时机，不是『别推类似产品』，similar products 是录音没有的偷换。  借用原文：If you post too many promotions early on, you will turn many people off
